sentences.text: This meeting is being recorded.
Hey, Andy, how are you?
I'm good, thank you.
Cliff, apologies for the late arrival.
Thank you for being whereabouts.
You guys.
It happens.
No worries.
I'm based in Manhattan, New York City.
How about you?
Ah, yeah, we're in Somerset, which in the southwest of England.
It's about an hour and a half from the.
From London.
We're actually officially based in London, but.
Okay, cool.
Nice.
That's awesome.
It's everywhere.
I.
I love it.
I've been to London a few times.
It's been a lot of years, but I'm.
I'm overdue to go back.
Yeah, I know.
Listen, I know that we have only this 15 minute window scheduled right now.
If it'll be helpful to follow up later on, I'm always happy to spend more time, but can given we only have these 12 minutes now, do you want me just to dive right into it and kind of tell you?
Yeah, just really, these sort of short calls are just to work out what it is that you're looking to do.
So we know whether we can help you or not and we can certainly book another call and deep dive into it if we can.
Okay, cool.
Yeah, let's jump straight into it because I can see you guys are obviously looking to sell.
You've got some great momentum and looks like you've got some size already to the business.
So.
Yeah, yeah.
Which is exciting.
And, and I, I was able to.
Yeah, I'll.
We can focus in on me giving you more details.
I was able to look up you guys a lot and I think I have a good, good idea of what you do.
So.
So there, there are kind of two things, Andy, that, that are top of mind for me is that sometime in the coming years we are going to want to exit.
And, and so I'm trying to build relationships in advance with M and A firms that, that I would love to be our partner to.
To facilitate that exit whenever the time comes and also to be my like, thought partner in terms of like.

Oh, Cliff, like you, you should, you know, you should wait even longer because you guys are on this crazy growth trajectory and you want to have a bigger exit or basically a thought partner around the timing.
So that's the first thing that, that like, I would love to continue the conversation on.
And then secondly, there's also this like, immediate thing that I'm in need of, which is that I need.
Have you ever heard of ypo?
Young Professionals Organization?
Does that ring a bell?
I was nominated to join YPO.
It's, you know, it's basically this network of CEOs or founders across the world.
And it's, it's an amazing opportunity if you join ypo because it's a great networking opportunity and it would be a total game changer for me if I'm able to join it.
I've heard amazing things about it.
But the thing about YPO is even though I got nominated and recommended and it's looking good, in order to join them, they have certain minimum requirements for your business.
One of the minimum requirements is that your business, you need to prove that.
I need to prove that we have a current enterprise value.

So basically just like our hypothetical valuation right now of, of at least $25 million, which I think we are above, but that they told me that I just need to get a third party to, to it could, it can literally just be like one sheet with letterhead, with company letterhead on it, whatever.
So that's also like, candidly, that's immediate.
That's like an immediate need that I'd be, I'd be happy to pay for that as well, but I, we would charge for it.
Yeah, I mean I can give you a valuation now.
So you said 3 to 5 million EBITDA?
Yeah, yeah, exactly.
At the moment our projection for this year for 2025 is to be between 6 and 7 million revenue and then to 3 and 3.5 million EBITDA.
So our margin is quite high and our growth trajectory is very, very strongly.
We're basically doubling year over year ever since 2021.

Another really promising thing is that we have direct partnerships with a lot of private equity funds and then we act as the go to marketing agency for their, their portfolio companies and we even have a contract signed directly with funds that say like, oh, you're the go to marketing partner.
So some examples are like TPG or General Catalyst or.
And then there's a lot of others based in New York City.
But so yeah, some of the biggest private equity funds in the world, we are their go to partner.
And so basically it's like a guaranteed ongoing stream of new clients for us that they're going to keep.
So I'm just giving you examples of like, there's a lot of other tailwinds that I think could help.
What do you do with them?
What's, what's like your forte?
So they, they, they buy in these companies and then you will help them grow through marketing.
That's exactly right.
And, and the reason that we've got that we are so good at this is that my co Founder and I both worked at Google for many years earlier in our careers we focused on digital marketing the entire time.
So we ran the digital marketing for like Verizon, Etsy and Dell and Snapchat, all these brands.
And then after that I was the chief growth officer for a company and I, so I ran all the marketing for a long time for a company and then we founded this business.
So that, so what you said is exactly right.
We, we are an agency that we do all the media buying so we manage and deploy all the marketing dollars on behalf of our clients.
So we work with the CMOs of these companies and our revenue is all recurring.
It's all recurring.
So we sign like, we sign long term contracts with, with all of our clients.
And so you know, the same way as if we were like a SaaS product, like we, we get recurring revenue from every company on a monthly basis.
And that's, that's great because it makes it very predictable and, and our MRR just keeps growing of course, every, every month.
Yeah.
Amazing.
Yeah.
So I know I'm so, I'm giving you, I'm giving you the pitch here as to why.
So I know another company that's in this, this space and they are looking to merge or be acquired as well.
So it's quite interesting.
Yeah, I'm really interested in this space obviously because it's, it's our space too.
So.
Yeah, yeah, totally.
So, yeah, okay.
So.
Right, just, well let me, let me answer you quickly.
So just on the, the valuation you're probably somewhere between sort of seven to nine, let's say.

So a 7.5 times multiple, you're at the bottom end of that, that range I would say just because of the size, but I've not looked into the business, I've not pulled your financials apart, but certainly would be able to hang my hat on a valuation roughly around 26 and a quarter mil.
That'd be amazing because that's all I need to be able to send them.
And again I would be down to pay you for that.
So I mean in order for me to put that on a headed paper.
Yeah, we do charge for that, but not just because going to put it on the paper but because we would have to look at it a bit more than me just saying that's what you're worth.
So we charged two and a half thousand dollars for that.
I don't know, that's out of your range or you're looking for somebody to just stick the name on the top of something.
I'm Obviously happy to do that.
If we can look at the business a little bit more and confirm that that's the price.
So if you can confirm that that would be the price.
The, the 26.
As long as it's not.
If it's north of 25 million, I, I'll pay you to, I'll pay you today, the two and a half day.
All right, I'll, I'll send you the details then in terms of, in terms of the other stuff.
So you're saying that your, your goal is for this to be quite far out.
It's not like something you're looking to do in the next few years.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
Frankly that, that's, I think that's right.
Because I would love, I would love for.
My goal is to, is to sell this for, you know, over $300 million, this company and perhaps maybe half a billion.
And if you are a partner doing that, I think that, I think that you would want the same.
Right, because you guys, I think that you guys bill on.
You guys charge on a percentage of exit price, right?
Yeah, of course.
The bigger the better.
But obviously if you're exiting a half a million, a half billion.
Sorry, I'm going to have to wait.
So.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
Any, any browner this.
Yeah, yeah.
So the fastest way for you to get there, Cliff, is through acquisitions.
I don't know that you've got anybody else coaching you or telling you how to get there, but obviously, you know, you know Google really well.
Google didn't just grow organically.
They made lots of really smart acquisitions.
Probably, you know, half of their revenue don't know exact numbers, but probably coming from YouTube, but they didn't build it themselves.
So.
Right.
That's a really good example of, of how you get there as quickly as possible.
Same with Facebook, some same with Apple.
Everybody bought stuff to get, to get to where they wanted to get.
If you want to build it organically, you're looking at 10 times longer window to get there.
It's a really good call out.
It's a really good call out.
And there are tons of smaller agencies that are looking to get acquired that we could acquire.
And there's also agencies that are doing something that we're not yet doing yet.
So a brand new revenue stream for us that we can acquire and then just integrate with our existing client base of 75, 60 clients, 100%.
And that's the way to grow as well because there's something else called multiple arbitrage.
So looking at, with those smaller agencies, you're buying them at 3 to 5x but they're immediately worth 7.5x as soon as they join your company.
Because you're a big, you trade for a bigger multiple.
So you're actually just creating value that isn't there.
And in terms of your timeline, instead of waiting, you know, 10, 20 years to build out to get to half a billion, you can get them much quicker.
You're just adding on these companies that you're paying this much for and they're worth this much.
And actually as you all grow together, your multiple goes up as well.
So you know, once you get into the sort of 5, 8 million EBITDA, you then start to get to the sort of 9 to 12 times multiple.
So yes, just keep adding that EBITDAR on doesn't have to be organic at all.
But from the perspective of another buyer, they're happy to pay much bigger multiples for what you're, you're, you're selling.
So you know, if you can get up to 10 million EBITDA through acquisitions and it can be just a bunch, you know, five small ones, then then you can get to that valuation much sooner.
Obviously you've got your site set on a massive number, which is great.
I, I, I, I, I do and I'm very happy we're having this conversation actually.

It's, it's, it's more, it's more insightful than, you know, I, I've obviously thought a lot about at what point we want to start acquiring smaller, smaller firms that would be centered, synergistic with us.
But, but just hearing, giving all your experience in the space and then hearing your hearing you flat out just say that.
It is.
Yeah.
And I've also thought a lot about if we have a software component, right, Particularly with the prominence of AI now, I think we'd be able to build it or acquire it more quickly than ever.
Some kind of software that's client facing and revenue generating, then I think it helps in a couple of ways.
We can improve the efficiency of our operations.
So like our EBITDA can get better just inherently because we have, we're getting more efficient.
Secondly, it's a new revenue stream because we can charge clients for software in addition to our services.
And then thirdly, my understanding is that your multiple can go up if you're selling software in addition to just like the service.
So we sold a company last year, Leaders, to Stagwell.
So Leaders is an Israeli influencer marketing agency, Stagwell's US company.
We had a multiple for their agency Business, which was bigger than the software component, but the software business was in the double digits mid, sort of around the 13, 14.
And, and, and, and, and if they hadn't had any software, the agency's multiple would have just been more probably like 10, right.
Six, seven.
You know, it's much lower multiples, so of course, yeah, you'll get a better multiple.
But actually it carried the software component, carried the whole business.
You know, the agency got an uplift as well.
So yeah, comes a lot more attractive.
So definitely, if you can add the software component.
The thing is, and I talked to loads of founders that think if they've built it and it sits inside the business, that there's value, but there's only value.
Like you say, if you're running clients through it and it's generating revenue, that's, that's where the real value is.
So that's the direction to go in.
So how about I send you an email and we can, we can get the valuation done for you.
Happy to do that.

And then the other track, which is really about making acquisitions, I think probably takes another conversation where we can get into it and I can, yeah, I can break down for you how we would be able to work and accelerate that for you.
That'd be fantastic.
Let's, let's rock and roll.
Let's do it.
I can have my EA reach out to you and, and schedule times, whether it's next week or the following.
We can continue the broader conversation.
And then in the meantime, Andy.
Yeah.
If, if you can email me, let me know what, what you think.
If you can say, hey, Cliff, if we do the exercise, we'd be able to get you that 26.
You think the 26 million valuation or what you said, then I'll, I'll immediately pay the two and a half K.
I would love that.
So thank you.
Times 3.5 is what I'd be working on.
And if that's where you genuinely are going to hit this year, then absolutely happy to put that.
That's the projection.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
All right.
Amazing.
I love it.
Cool.
All right, well, good to meet you.
Flying visit.
Maybe longer next time.
I will.
So do we also need another sync on the calendar just to discuss the, this, the immediate exercise?
No, no, no, we can just do that.
No, that's fine.
We just need you to send the financials over.
So we'll just have to look were last year where you're at this year and then just agree.
Yeah, that looks really genuine.
Okay.
All right, amazing.
Thank you so much.
I appreciate it.
Andy, great to meet you and excited to continue the discussion.
Yeah, me too, Cliff.
Have a great day.

summary.overview: In a concise Business Development and M&A Consultation meeting, Cliff Simmons from Manhattan and Andy Day from Somerset engaged in a focused discussion about Cliff's strategic business objectives. Cliff is seeking an immediate valuation document to help join the Young Professionals Organization, with a minimum target of $25 million, and is interested in establishing partnerships with M&A firms for a future exit strategy. Andy provided insight into Cliff’s digital marketing agency, projecting a future revenue of $6-7 million and discussing its strong performance and recurring revenue model. He offered a valuation estimate of approximately $26.25 million, along with formal service for $2,500, emphasizing the potential for growth through acquisitions. The meeting concluded with agreed next steps, including follow-up communication regarding the valuation and scheduling further discussions on acquisition strategies, pending the provision of necessary financial documentation from Cliff.
summary.short_summary: Cliff Simmons from Manhattan and Andy Day from Somerset engaged in a focused consultation regarding Cliff's strategic business objectives, particularly his need for an immediate third-party valuation document to secure membership in the Young Professionals Organization (YPO), targeting a minimum valuation of $25 million. Andy provided insights into Cliff's digital marketing agency, projecting future revenues of $6-7 million and discussing its strong performance driven by recurring revenue. He estimated a valuation of approximately $26.25 million, with a formal valuation service offered at $2,500. They discussed growth strategies, particularly the potential for acquisitions to enhance value and the importance of integrating smaller agencies for higher multiples. The meeting concluded with agreed next steps, including follow-up communications and financial document submissions.
